title: Stress whispers

captions.ayurpetofficial:
Your dog won't always bark or hide when they're stressed. Sometimes it whispers. 🐾

Diwali is 20 days away, so learn the quiet signs now, before the crackers start: a yawn when they're not tired, a quick lip lick, panting without exercise, a full body shake after a tense moment, and freezing. That last one means "I don't feel safe."

Amanda Ree of @samadogwellbeing shows you each one.

Send this to the friend whose dog "is just being difficult." Next from Amanda: 3 points that calm them.

title: Three calming points

captions.ayurpetofficial:
Crackers, the doorbell that won't stop, a house full of guests. 3 pressure points that can help your dog settle, from Amanda Ree of @samadogwellbeing:

1. Third eye, between the eyes just above the nose: a steady, gentle press for 20 to 30 seconds
2. Base of the ears, behind the ear flaps: very light pressure for 15 to 20 seconds
3. Base of the tail: gentle circles for 20 to 30 seconds

Save this for Diwali night. Go gently, watch their body language and stop if they pull away. Pain, limping or anything sudden goes to your vet first.

#AyurPet #AyurvedaForPets #DogParentsIndia #DogsOfIndia #IndieDogs #DiwaliWithPets

title: Where your dog holds stress (shoulder massage)

captions.ayurpet_global:
Your dog carries stress in their shoulders, just like you do. 🐾

Anxious, fearful, can't settle when you leave? Try Amanda Ree's shoulder massage (@samadogwellbeing):
1. Palms on the shoulder blades. Press gently, moving under and around them
2. Found a tight spot or a small knot? Hold light pressure for 5 to 10 seconds
3. Watch how your dog responds. A sigh means you're on the right track

Save this for your dog's next hard day. Send it to someone whose dog can't switch off.

Gentle care, not a treatment. If your dog is in pain, limping or recovering from surgery, see your vet first.

title: How to fix your dog's gut, explained like you're five (GoodGut+ v2.1, 2:02)
approved: Karan 2026-11-12 in chat: post today to both IG accounts + FB page, caption approved as drafted, no AI line

captions.ayurpetofficial:
How to fix your dog's gut, explained like you're five 🐶

Eating grass, licking paws, loose stools. Most of the time it isn't a skin problem. It starts in the gut.

A happy gut needs three things:
1. Break food down (digestive enzymes)
2. Calm the gut (triphala, milk thistle, bhumi amla)
3. Feed the good bacteria (prebiotics from banana, pumpkin, sweet potato and chicory root)

GoodGut+ does all three. A few drops a day, mixed into his food, and dogs love the taste.

Save this, and send it to a dog parent whose dog won't stop licking his paws 🧡

If the tummy trouble keeps going, check in with your vet. Link in bio.

title: Where older dogs hold pain (lower back massage)
status: HOLD: new Amanda reel, needs Karan's written OK. Set READY only after his yes.

captions.ayurpet_global:
Older dogs hold a lot of their pain in the lower back. 🐾

It supports nearly every move they make, so it's where arthritis, stiffness and hip trouble show up, especially in larger breeds. Amanda Ree of @samadogwellbeing shows a gentle massage for it:
1. Start near the spine, just behind the lower ribs. Rub slow circles with your palms
2. Never press on the spine itself
3. Move down to the glutes. Squeeze gently, then release
4. Finish with a slow sweep down the hips and legs

About five minutes on each side is plenty.

Save this for your older dog. Send it to someone whose dog is slowing down.

title: Where older dogs hold pain (lower back massage)
status: HOLD: new Amanda reel, needs Karan's written OK. Set READY only after his yes.

captions.ayurpetofficial:
Older dogs hold a lot of their pain in the lower back. 🐾

It supports nearly every move they make, so it's where arthritis, stiffness and hip trouble show up, especially in larger breeds. Amanda Ree of @samadogwellbeing shows a gentle massage for it:
1. Start near the spine, just behind the lower ribs. Rub slow circles with your palms
2. Never press on the spine itself
3. Move down to the glutes. Squeeze gently, then release
4. Finish with a slow sweep down the hips and legs

About five minutes on each side is plenty.

Save this for your older dog. Send it to someone whose dog is slowing down.

Gentle care, not a treatment. If your dog is in pain, limping or recovering from surgery, see your vet first.

Senior dogs don't complain. They just get quieter. Save this for a cold morning and send it to a senior dog parent.
